title: App lifecycle: pause, resume and background
when: The phone app loses unsaved input when it goes to the background, timers drift, or data looks stale when the user comes back.
inputs: timers or live connections in the app
prompt:
Goal: lifecycle.js saves state when the app is hidden, stops wasteful work in the background and refreshes cleanly on return.
Steps:
1. Listen to document "visibilitychange": when document.visibilityState is "hidden" call onPause(), when "visible" call onResume().
2. Also listen to "pagehide" for the last save; the phone may kill a hidden app without any further event.
3. In a Capacitor shell add App.addListener("appStateChange", ({ isActive }) => ...) and the "pause" and "resume" events.
4. onPause: write drafts to storage synchronously small or to IndexedDB, stop setInterval timers, close WebSocket connections, pause media.
5. onResume: compute elapsed time from Date.now() minus the saved pausedAt instead of trusting timers, refetch data older than 5 minutes, reopen connections.
6. If the app was killed, restore drafts and the last route on next launch.
7. Never depend on code running while hidden; real background work needs native background tasks or push.
Quality bar:
- Switching apps mid typing loses nothing.
- No timers or sockets run while hidden.
Pitfalls:
- Saving only in "beforeunload" or "unload", which phones often skip.
- Countdown timers that pause in the background and show wrong values.
- Refetching everything on each resume and draining data.
Verify:
- [ ] visibilitychange and pagehide both save.
- [ ] Timers stop on pause and restart on resume.
- [ ] Elapsed time uses timestamps.
Output: lifecycle.js and the hook calls in app.js.

examples.input: quando troco de app no celular perco o que digitei
examples.output: lifecycle.js: save on hidden and pagehide, stop timers, refresh stale data on resume
